about.title: Personal Injury Help in Millbrae, California
about.longDescription: Millbrae sits along some of the Peninsula's busiest travel corridors, and the traffic reflects it. In the most recent full year on record, the city logged 71 injury collisions and 98 people hurt, with no reported traffic deaths. Public crash data show reports clustering on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., and the corridors carrying the most reported collisions include El Camino Real, US-101, E Millbrae Avenue, and SR-82. Whether someone was rear-ended near the 101 interchange, sideswiped on El Camino Real, or hit while crossing E Millbrae Avenue, the aftermath is often the same: medical bills piling up, missed work, and a lot of unanswered questions. LawProactive is a free service that helps injured people in Millbrae connect with an independent personal injury attorney — we are not a law firm, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. Reaching out costs nothing and starts the process of understanding your options while evidence and memories are still fresh.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: The Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity like a city or transit agency is involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so early guidance matters.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Erase Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you're found partly responsible for a crash, you can still recover damages — just reduced by your share of fault. An attorney can help make sure your fault isn't overstated by an insurer.

items.title: No Cap on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California doesn't limit non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so these losses can be fully considered and valued.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to You
items.desc: Attorneys connected through LawProactive work on contingency, which means they only get paid if you recover money. There's no retainer and no bill just for asking questions.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: For most personal injury cases, California law allows two years from the date of the injury to file a lawsuit. If your claim involves a government entity, that deadline can be much shorter — sometimes just six months — so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to be reported in Millbrae?
items.answer: Public collision records show reported crashes clustering along El Camino Real, US-101, E Millbrae Avenue, and SR-82, with reports peaking on Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. These are simply public-record counts and not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you share some responsibility for the crash. Your recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it isn't automatically barred.
